Chronology 3 — The Flood and Noah

The Bible's text — what is actually said

  • God's grief: "the LORD was sorry that He had made man… and was grieved in His heart" (Gen 6:6) — strongly anthropopathic language (cf. the cap. 09 / cap. 10 contrast with Q 50:38's transcendence).
  • Noah "found grace" (6:8); precise ark instructions; 40 days of rain, waters prevailing 150 days; all flesh dies except eight souls — Noah, his wife, his three sons (Shem, Ham, Japheth) and their wives. The whole household is saved.
  • The raven and the dove; the altar; God "smelled the pleasing aroma" and resolved "never again" (8:21).
  • The Noahic covenant (Gen 9): universal, with all humanity and every creature, sealed by the bow in the cloud — a covenant of preservation/common grace. (Gen 9:20–27, the drunkenness and the curse of Canaan, is a separate, much-abused text; noted neutrally, not germane to the flood comparison.)

The Qur'an's text — what is actually said

  • Nuh preaches "950 years" (Q 29:14) and is mocked while building the ark (Q 11:38); builds it under inspiration (Q 11:37).
  • Onset signal: "the oven gushed forth" (fāra al-tannūr, Q 11:40); the ark "ran amid waves like mountains" (Q 11:42); at the end the command "O earth, swallow your water; O sky, withhold" (Q 11:44).
  • The son-dialogue is given in full: the son says "I will take refuge on a mountain"; he drowns (Q 11:42–43). Noah pleads "my son is of my family"; God corrects him — "he is not of your family; it is an unrighteous deed; ask Me not of that you know nothing of" (Q 11:45–46); Noah repents (11:47). (Even a prophet is here corrected — touching the 'isma question; flagged as a textual datum, not resolved.)
  • Noah's wife is a Qurʾanic parable of the unbelieving spouse, paired with Lot's wife (Q 66:10) — lost though married to a prophet.
  • Scope (global vs. local) is left open and debated in tafsir.

Collision

The decisive divergence is who was saved:

BibleQur'an
Noah's wifesavedlost (Q 66:10)
Noah's sonsall three savedone son drowns (Q 11:43)
Salvation principlehousehold / lineagefaith over kinship

The Qur'an's version is internally purposeful: it dramatizes the cap. 11 principle — no one is saved by family tie; each stands on personal faith ("he is not of your family; his conduct is unrighteous", Q 11:46). It reads as a theological correction of Genesis's household-salvation motif, fully consistent with Q 35:18 and Ezek 18:20 — note the Qurʾan is here more consistent with the shared individual-responsibility principle than Genesis's household model is.

The shared external problem — Mesopotamian flood traditions

Symmetry requires naming a difficulty that lands on both texts: mainstream scholarship sees the Genesis flood as literarily related to older Mesopotamian accounts (the Gilgamesh XI tablet, Atrahasis, Ziusudra) — shared motifs: the warned righteous man, the ark, the birds sent out, the mountain landing, the sacrifice. The Qurʾanic account, being later, inherits the same tradition-stream.

This is presented neutrally, not as a weapon: it is a common external pressure (Methodology §3, §5). It does not favour either scripture against the other, and the arbiter does not rule on literary dependence vs. independent memory of a real event — out of remit.

Two theological functions

The divergence is not only "who survived" but what the story is for:

  • Bible → covenant of preservation. The flood culminates in the Noahic covenant with all humanity and creation (the rainbow): a theology of common grace and divine restraint ("never again").
  • Qurʾan → serialized warning. Nuh is the first in a repeating "warner" pattern (Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Lūṭ, Shuʿayb): a messenger is mocked, the people are destroyed, the faithful saved. The flood is one episode in a didactic series on rejecting prophets, not the seal of a universal covenant.

Both are internally coherent; they are different literary-theological machines built from the same raw narrative.

Arbiter verdict — the Flood

Present. Shared event (righteous Noah, ark, deluge, deliverance); divergent on the survivors and on the principle the story teaches.

Weigh.

  • Symmetric, out of remit: a global flood is rejected by mainstream geology/archaeology, and the Mesopotamian parallels pressure the Genesis account's originality — both pressures fall on the two texts together (Methodology §3, §5) and decide nothing between them.
  • Real divergence, internally consistent: the lost son and wife are deliberate in the Qurʾan, locking the flood onto the same individual-responsibility seam as the Fall — and arguably more consistent with the shared Ezek 18 / Q 35:18 principle than Genesis's household salvation.
  • Different machines: covenant-of-preservation (Bible) vs. serialized warner-pattern (Qurʾan) — a structural, not cosmetic, difference.

Judge. On historicity and originality: a wash — both face the same external problems; no winner. On internal-principle consistency: a narrow point to the Qurʾan — its faith-over-kinship outcome aligns better with the individual-responsibility axiom both scriptures elsewhere affirm, whereas Genesis's whole-household salvation sits in mild tension with its own Ezek 18. On theological function: not better/worse but different by design (covenant vs. warning-series), each coherent. No evidentiary winner overall; a clear, traceable continuation of the seam.
